claims.claim: The Koopman-closure evaluation-state construction exactly generates every future trajectory of every declared readout.
Predictive equivalence is the coarsest deterministic state equivalence preserving all future declared readouts.
Every reachable exact linear realization surjects onto the predictive realization; minimal reachable exact linear realizations are isomorphic.
In finite-dimensional cases, generalized future-readout Hankel rank equals minimal predictive realization dimension.

For a finite system with all scalar functions available as readouts, the deterministic predictive quotient is the reachable orbit machine and the minimal linear predictive dimension equals the number of reachable states.
For linear dynamics and linear readouts, the predictive realization is the reachable subspace modulo the reachable unobservable subspace.
For finite-state Markov kernels, the observable-semigroup construction yields the minimal reachable linear realization of all expected future declared readouts under the declared controls.
A full path-law minimality theorem requires a richer observable class or direct experiment-law equivalence and is not established here.
For a declared semigroup of deterministic control generators, Koopman closure under all control words yields a minimal reachable linear realization of all declared controlled future readouts.
The universal minimality proof depends only on a semigroup of linear operators on observables, declared source functionals, and a declared readout subspace.
